title: Extreme poverty remains widespread as social protection expands unevenly against rising costs and compound shocks
source_unit: United Nations Statistics Division, Sustainable Development Goals Report 2026, Goal 1: No Poverty
geography: Global country and regional SDG 1 reporting across poverty, social protection, aid, and vulnerability indicators

denominator.unit: world population under the 2021 PPP extreme-poverty line

extreme_poverty_share.unit: percent of the world population estimated to live in extreme poverty

extreme_poverty_count.unit: million people estimated to live in extreme poverty

threshold.unit: US dollars per person per day in 2021 purchasing-power-parity terms

observations.method: UNSD compilation of global and regional SDG 1 poverty estimates using the internationally comparable monetary poverty line.
observations.uncertainty: Global poverty estimates depend on survey coverage, purchasing-power adjustments, interpolation, modeling, and the selected threshold; they do not measure multidimensional deprivation or insecurity completely.
observations.subgroup: People in low-income and fragile settings, children, rural populations, workers with low or unstable earnings, and households exposed to conflict or climate shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: The estimate is a global benchmark rather than a complete account of material living standards; progress can occur above or below the line without changing other dimensions of well-being.

denominator.unit: people classified as vulnerable in countries reporting social-assistance coverage

coverage.unit: percent of vulnerable persons covered by social assistance in 2026

policy_role.value: non-contributory, tax-financed benefits are identified as a tool for reducing poverty and vulnerability

observations.method: UNSD synthesis of SDG social-protection and social-assistance indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage does not establish adequacy, duration, take-up, delivery quality, exclusion errors, or whether benefits keep pace with food, housing, energy, and care costs.
observations.subgroup: Low-income households, children, older people, people with disabilities, unemployed workers, caregivers, migrants, and people outside contributory systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: A 10.6-point expansion represents meaningful institutional growth even if coverage remains incomplete and uneven across countries.

grant_change.unit: percent change in poverty-reduction ODA grants between 2023 and 2024

delivery_implication.value: financing constraints can narrow fiscal room for social protection and poverty-reduction programs

observations.method: UNSD compilation of official-development-assistance flows classified for poverty reduction.
observations.uncertainty: Aid classification and annual flows do not reveal program effectiveness, domestic financing substitution, allocation quality, or longer-term fiscal capacity.
observations.subgroup: Low-income countries, fragile settings, social-protection agencies, communities dependent on externally financed services, and households facing crisis shocks.
observations.counterinterpretation: Domestic revenue, borrowing, remittances, and redesigned programs can partly offset lower grants in particular countries.

denominator.unit: global SDG 1 risk and policy frame

driver_set.value: inequality, climate shocks, conflict, and rising living costs continue to push people into poverty

policy_set.value: inclusive economic opportunity and stronger social protection are identified as core responses

data_boundary.value: poverty monitoring depends on timely, comparable, and sufficiently covered household and administrative data

observations.method: UNSD SDG 1 synthesis linking poverty, distribution, social protection, shocks, living costs, and statistical capacity.
observations.uncertainty: The report describes cross-domain risk pathways but does not estimate a single causal contribution for each shock or policy response.
observations.subgroup: Households with low buffers, informal workers, people in conflict-affected or climate-exposed places, and populations missed by statistical systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Growth, labor-market access, public services, transfers, and resilience investments can interact to reduce poverty even when one channel deteriorates.

related_sources.claim: World Bank Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet provides complementary poverty, inequality, climate-risk, and shared-prosperity context.
World Bank poverty-line update provides complementary methodology for global income and consumption thresholds.

boundary: This record adds a current aggregate poverty-and-protection route linking consumption thresholds, social assistance, aid, living costs, climate, conflict, and data capacity. It is not a household panel, individual benefit-take-up study, respondent-level consumption dataset, or causal estimate of any single shock.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UNSD 2026 Goal 1 page was reviewed; poverty, social-assistance, aid, compound-shock, and data-capacity claims were cross-checked.
